subject: SDK graceful drain API & prefetch opt-out request for low-RTO customers
messages:
From: Sarah Thomas <sarah.thomas@novapay.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeOps Support <eng@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: Demo failure & logs — SDK connection drain causing trailing latency spikes

Hi Priyom / Lauren,

During yesterday's sandbox demo we hit a reproducible failure where the client SDK's connection drain process appears to trigger a long tail of token latency (5-15s) for short requests after a scale-down. The attached logs and a short screen clip show the pattern — the request itself completes but the session-level prefetch/kv cache refresh overlaps with subsequent requests and delays the short, latency-sensitive path.

Impact: NovaPay has a couple of end-user flows that need <150ms RTO for small prompts. These spikes caused the demo to look flaky and they asked for a path forward. They also asked whether we can opt-out prefetch/kv-cache refresh on a per-customer basis until they accept an SLA with dedicated capacity.

Attachments: novapay_logs_oct18.zip (kernel traces + client logs), prefetch_trace_100318.txt, demo_fail_clip.mp4

Can someone from platform/runtime confirm: 1) is there a known drain-triggered refresh that is synchronous on the request path; 2) can we expose a per-API flag (or SDK config) to disable background prefetch during drain or short-circuit it for low-RTO customers?

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Thomas
Director, Integrations — NovaPay

Looping in Karthik and Logan to assess runtime/SDK surface. Quick context for product: NovaPay is asking for a per-tenant opt-out of prefetch/kv-cache refresh during drain or an explicit SDK flag — they need it as an interim mitigation while we evaluate Dedicated capacity.

Ask for Product/Runtime:
- Small API: expose an SDK config (client-side) and/or server-side flag to mark a connection as "low-latency" which avoids synchronous prefetch on drain.
- If server-side: we need a safe default that doesn't weaken cache hit rates for others; possibly a policy that only affects short-prompts (<32 tokens) or explicit tenant opt-out.
- Roadmap impact: is this a simple feature we can ship as a config toggle (1-2 sprints) or does it require kernel/runtime changes?

From a Sales Eng perspective I want to offer NovaPay a documented temporary config we can enable for their sandbox and a path to Canary the change. Please advise on risk and rollout steps.

Attaching the log bundle they sent.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeOps Support <eng@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo failure & logs — SDK connection drain causing trailing latency spikes

Thanks for the signal and logs — dumped them into INF-2147. Summary of our initial findings:
- The runtime has an opportunistic prefix/kv prefetch that can run inline in the same worker thread during a connection drain path when memory pressure causes earlier evictions. In the current implementation the prefetch can block the next request if the worker hasn't yielded. That explains the 5-15s tail in those traces.
- It's configuration-driven at two levels: SDK-side hint (prefetch_hint) and runtime policy (prefetch_on_drain = true). The SDK hint is best-effort; the runtime policy is authoritative. Currently we don't expose a tenant-scoped override in control plane.

Proposed triage and short-term mitigations (recommended order):
1) Server-side tenant opt-out behind a dynamic feature flag: prefetch_on_drain=false for tenant NovaPay. This is low-risk and we can flip it per-tenant; requires a config path in control plane + runtime read. Estimated 2-3 days for a canary deploy + validation.
2) SDK-side addition: a lightweight config param (sdk.no_prefetch_on_drain = true) that sends a header to the control plane — trivial SDK change (1 sprint) and compatible with existing runtime check.
3) Graceful yield path: change the runtime worker to pre-empt prefetch when the next short request arrives (non-blocking prefetch). This requires a kernel-level change and careful perf validation — medium risk, 2-3 sprints.

I recommend we do 1) immediately for the NovaPay sandbox, ship 2) in the SDK next sprint for broader customer opt-outs, and schedule 3) on the runtime roadmap (post-sprint planning) as a performance improvement.

Risk notes: per-tenant opt-out will reduce cache effectiveness for that tenant and could increase per-token cost in dedicated scenarios. We'll document the tradeoff in the customer-facing KB.

I'll create an INF ticket with the canary steps and validation metrics (tail-latency percentiles for prompts <32 tokens). Need a sign-off from Product for the config path and from Security for any control-plane flag exposure.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks all — read INF-2147 and the proposed plan. I agree with the 3-step approach and can commit the following operational path so Sales can give NovaPay a concrete timeline:

Immediate (canary within 72 hours):
- Control-plane per-tenant flag "prefetch_on_drain=false" will be plumbed into the runtime. I'll own the canary rollout on the hosted fleet for the NovaPay sandbox cluster. Validation: compare p50/p95/p99 for short prompts (<32 tokens) before/after for 24h.

Short term (SDK next release, ~2 weeks):
- Add sdk.no_prefetch_on_drain header and document SDK config. This gives customers a supported client-side approach. QA will validate cross-language SDKs.

Medium term (runtime improvement, 2-3 sprints):
- Implement non-blocking prefetch/yield on workers. We'll run perf tests on staging (multi-tenant) to ensure no regressions.

Product asks for sign-off:
- Lauren: can you confirm we can expose a tenant-scoped runtime flag in the control plane UI/privileged API? We should also surface expected cost delta and a short KB article for customers.
- Security: we'll follow the same audit/logging for feature flags; no additional data plane exposure is needed.

Priyom, please tell NovaPay we can do the canary in the next 48-72 hours if they share a sandbox tenant id and confirm they accept the tradeoff (possible cache miss rate increase). We'll also provide a demo repro checklist so Sales can validate immediately after the canary.

Action items:
- Priyom: collect sandbox tenant id + confirm demo window
- Lauren: product sign-off for tenant flag path and KB blurb
- Karthik: create INF-2147 subtasks for the canary + SDK change
- Logan: schedule canary and monitoring (I'll post the runbook link)

Thanks — Logan
Product Manager, Platform
